correctness.rationale: For every t>=2 and every vector of clique orders r_i>=2, the center-in and center-out proof derives necessary and sufficient occupancy conditions from the original open-neighborhood total domination and one-guard exchange predicates. Center-in requires every blade met: attacking a vertex in an empty blade forces center removal and isolates the attacking vertex; any nonempty blade supplies an internal defender. Center-out requires at least two per blade already for total domination, and these occupancy counts are maintained by every allowed rim attack; an attack on the center removes one guard from a blade with at least two, so all blades remain met and the new center is totally dominated. The two disjoint cases yield the complete product polynomial. Deleting guards to the minimum allowed counts proves the inclusion-minimal polynomial, and both positivity products give exactly two minimal cardinalities. Independent adjacency checks (verify.py) tested 127904 vertex subsets on 66 vectors and all expected coefficients. The infinite result depends on the proof, not the finite tests.

value.rationale: Relocation-robust total domination is a motivated graph-protection problem, and clique bouquets are an infinite natural connected chordal block-graph/cograph class with arbitrary heterogeneous blade sizes. The full all-set polynomial and all inclusion-minimal-set polynomial contain information not deducible from scalar gamma_st bounds. The theorem also provides an explicit family whose inclusion-minimal secure-total-dominating cardinality spectrum has two isolated values t+1 and 2t with t-2 missing intermediate sizes, unbounded on connected chordal graphs. This gives a structural boundary for possible minimal-set spectra rather than merely a renamed parameter or a table of finite calculations.
